newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tokobank plans EuroCP, ADRs next year.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tokobank plans EuroCP, ADRs next year.

text.p: One of Russia's biggest commercial banks, AKB Tokobank, plans to issue Eurocommercial paper and American Depositary Receipts, bank officials said on Tuesday.

Tokobank had signed an agreement with a Western bank on the general terms of the Eurocommercial paper issue and it will take this bank about two months to finalise the deal, Vladimir Smirnov, medium-term funds department head, told Reuters.
The bank plans to issue American Depositary Receipts next year, he said, adding the bank was not in a hurry to issue them.

Three other big Russian banks, Menatep, AB Inkombank and MAKB Vozrozhdeniye have already received permission from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and Russian central bank to issue Level One ADRs.

Tokobank has issued $150 million worth of promissory notes to Western banks since the start of a programme at the end of last year, chairman Vyacheslav Khokhlov said. The bank's notes were backed by import and export contracts, he said.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has a 9.58 percent stake in Tokobank, Russian oil company Yuganskneftegaz 12.47 percent and Russia's biggest bank, Sberbank, 5.57 percent.
Tokobank's assets equalled 9.85 trillion roubles on November 1, 1996.
It has equity investments in Ost-West Handelsbank AG, Russian-Turkish bank Yapi-Tokobank, Russian Project Finance Bank and others.
